title: Bayesian models, priors, and posterior laws

items.title: Bayesian model as a prior and sampling kernel
items.statement: A proper Bayesian model is a prior probability on a measurable parameter space paired with a parameter-measurable sampling probability kernel representing the statistical experiment.
items.strategy: Definition only: specify the measurable parameter and data spaces, proper prior, sampling kernel, and representation equation; state that an indexed experiment alone does not supply parameter measurability.

items.title: Bayesian posterior as a regular conditional law
items.statement: A posterior RCD is the sample-point-indexed regular conditional distribution of the parameter coordinate given the data sigma-algebra; a data-indexed posterior is a separate probability kernel on the data space whose composition satisfies the same conditional identities.
items.strategy: Definition only: distinguish the canonical product-space RCD from a data-indexed conditional kernel, state the joint-law identity, and record null-fibre version freedom and the separate dominated-density route.

items.title: Posterior RCD exists for a standard-Borel parameter
items.statement: Under AC, a proper Bayesian model with standard-Borel parameter space has a posterior RCD given the data sigma-algebra, without a standard-Borel assumption on the data space.
items.strategy: Construct the prior-predictive joint law, identify the measurable parameter coordinate, and instantiate the standard-Borel-target RCD existence theorem with the data sigma-algebra.

items.title: Standard-Borel Bayesian posterior kernel exists
items.statement: Under AC, when both parameter and data spaces are standard Borel, the posterior RCD factors through the data as a measurable probability kernel, unique up to one prior-predictive null set.
items.strategy: Form the prior-predictive joint law, obtain the parameter RCD, factor it through the standard-Borel data coordinate, and use disintegration uniqueness for the null-set qualification.

title: Bayesian models, priors, and posterior laws — Examples

items.title: A finite Bayesian update and a null-data posterior version
items.statement: A two-parameter finite model gives posterior probabilities 1/7 and 3/5 for two positive-mass data values, while a zero-mass value admits distinct posterior versions.
items.strategy: Compute joint and predictive masses, normalize on positive-mass fibres, and verify the conditional rectangle identity including the zero-mass fibre.

items.title: A Bayesian posterior RCD indexed by the sample point
items.statement: In a symmetric binary-noise model the posterior RCD is a random probability measure on the canonical sample space, and its value is the data-indexed posterior at the observed coordinate.
items.strategy: Compute the four joint masses and data marginals, define the sample-point kernel by composition with the data coordinate, and verify every conditioning event in sigma(Y).

items.title: A dominated posterior on a nonstandard-Borel observation space
items.statement: A finite-prior model on the eight-set sigma-algebra generated by three nonempty atoms cannot separate points within an atom and has a jointly measurable dominated likelihood with an explicit data-indexed posterior kernel.
items.strategy: Show the observation space is not standard Borel, normalize the two density sections, compute predictive density and posterior on all three atoms including the zero-evidence atom, and verify every rectangle identity.

items.title: A standard-Borel posterior kernel for countable data
items.statement: Two geometric sampling laws on countable discrete data give an explicit measurable posterior kernel that disintegrates the prior-predictive joint law.
items.strategy: Verify standard-Borel spaces and the normalized geometric likelihoods, apply the standard-Borel posterior theorem, and check the posterior rectangle identity term by term.
